h1: Hydraulic and rotary draw pipe benders — pipe, tube and bar to Ø3-1/8″
intro: A rotary draw bender clamps the tube to a rotating bend die and draws it around the die radius without an internal mandrel, and a hydraulic pipe bender bends pipe around a die with a hydraulic ram — the simplest machines for handrail, gate, fence, furniture, plumbing, exhaust and repair bends in pipe, tube and bar. NovoTech sells three lines in Canada, all on this page: ISITAN's BK series, four rotary draw benders from the 1 HP BK-42 for 1-1/4″ pipe to the BK 030 (76) for Ø3″ × 11 ga steel tube, bending pipe, tube, solid and flat bar and box section with one included tooling set; NovoTech's premium line, built in Turkey — the TB 34 electric bench bender for 1″ NPS pipe, the 17-ton hydraulic TB 42 for 1-1/4″ NPS pipe and the SPB 60 and SPB 76 NC draw benders with a 500-program memory for Ø2-3/8″ and Ø3″ pipe; and NovoTech's value line, built in China — the EHB-10 electric hydraulic pipe bender and the TB-3 and HTB-1000 benders for 2″ schedule 40 pipe, the HTB-25T 25-ton tubing bender and the TBM-60 electric bender to 2-1/2″, the HTB-2000 exhaust bender with an expander-swager and the JTB hydraulic PLC tube benders to Ø3-1/8″. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. For thin-wall tube to a tight radius, see the NC and CNC mandrel benders.

faq.a: A rotary draw bender clamps the tube to a bend die and draws it around; without an internal mandrel it suits thicker walls and radii of about 2× the diameter and up — handrail, gate, fence and furniture work. Thin-wall tube to a tight radius needs the mandrel support of an NC or CNC mandrel bender. The BK capacity table lists the maximum tube, bar and box section for each model.

The BK-050 bends Ø2-3/8″ × 14 ga 304/316 stainless tube and the BK-H 060 Ø2-3/8″ × 12 ga — the common 1-1/2″ and 2″ handrail sizes with room to spare. The hydraulic BK-H 060 draws from one direction, which makes sequential bends on long rails easier.

The BK benders come with one set — bend die, clamp die and counter die — in the size you request. Additional sets for other diameters, square tube, flat bar and box section are quoted with the machine; tell us material, size, wall, CLR and angle.

For the occasional bend in pipe up to 1-1/4″ NPS, the premium-line TB 34 (electric, digital angle stop) or TB 42 (17-ton hydraulic) is the simplest and lowest-cost premium machine. For railing, gate and furniture work in pipe, tube, bar and box section, the ISITAN BK series with its programmable controls and capacity to Ø3″ tube. For repeated multi-bend parts in pipe to Ø2-3/8″ or Ø3″, the SPB 60 or SPB 76 with a 500-program NC. Thin-wall tube to a tight radius needs a mandrel bender.

A rotary-draw bender (JTB, TBM-60, HTB-25T, TB-3, HTB-1000) pulls the tube around a die with a clamp and a follower — a tight, accurate bend with little flattening, the method for roll cages, railings, frames and exhaust. A push-type hydraulic pipe bender (EHB-10) pushes the pipe into a die between two supports — simple and fast for plumbing and electrical pipe, where some ovality is acceptable. For large radii, rings and spirals, see the tube rollers on the angle rolls page.

faq.q: What do I need to tell you to choose the dies?
faq.a: The outside diameter (or the square size), the wall thickness, the material and the centre-line radius (CLR) of the bend — usually 2 to 4 times the tube diameter. Tube and pipe sizes differ: 1-1/2″ schedule 40 pipe is 1.900″ OD, while 1-1/2″ tube is 1.500″ OD — the die must fit the OD exactly.

faq.q: What voltage do the benders run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on the BK-42 and other models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase.
